subject: MSA + Order Form: SLA items for review & fallback credits
body:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Luke Carr <luke@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: SLA items for review & fallback credits

Hi Luke —

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. As promised, I attached our current order form with the SLA redlines we discussed and a short credits spreadsheet that shows sample calculations under different outage windows. Key items we want to confirm with AtlasPay legal/procurement before routing to our legal team: 

- Uptime target (availability): 99.95% per calendar month for Redwood Hosted. For Dedicated/Private we can discuss a higher committed target per your needs.
- Service credits: tiered staircase tied to percentage downtime; proposal in SLA_credits_table.xlsx. Cap = 50% of monthly fees (we are flexible on cap for multi-year commits).
- Response times: P1 initial response 1 hour (business hours), P2 within 4 hours, P3 within 24 hours.
- Maintenance windows: we propose a regular weekly maintenance slot (Sunday 02:00–04:00 UTC) with 48h advance notice for scheduled work; emergency maintenance carveouts described in the doc.
- Fallbacks & routing: we propose an automated regional fallback policy in production for cross-region resilience; credits calculated based on the failing region's traffic share.

Attachments: Draft_OrderForm_redlines_v3.pdf, SLA_credits_table.xlsx, SLA_measurement_methodology.docx

Can you confirm AtlasPay’s appetite on availability (99.95 vs 99.99) and the credits cap? If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call with legal on Thursday.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message -----
From: Luke Carr <luke@atlaspay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:03:45 -0400
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: SLA items for review & fallback credits

Hannah —

Appreciate the draft. A few quick points from procurement/legal side after an initial pass:

1) AtlasPay will push for 99.99% for Production-critical payments; can Redwood offer a higher SLA for Dedicated/Private (we expect to move to Dedicated in year 2)?
2) Credits cap: 50% cap is aggressive — typical customers get 100% of 3 months fees in extreme cases. Can you explain the rationale for 50% and whether there are options to increase with a longer commitment?
3) Measurement: we need clear measurement windows and the traffic-share approach for multi-region fallbacks. Please provide a short methodology we can include for audit.
4) Maintenance: the proposed weekly slot is fine, but AtlasPay requires a 72-hour advance notice for any non-emergency maintenance that may affect transaction throughput.

I've attached our procurement redlines (sent separately). We should loop in our GC — she’s on copy on the procurement thread. Also need SOC 2 evidence + access to uptime dashboards for the pilot.

Can Marissa or Aditya weigh in on the Dedicated availability promise and measurement approach?

Best,
Luke
Director, Procurement
AtlasPay

----------
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 08:45:10 -0700
To: Luke Carr <luke@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: SLA items for review & fallback credits

Luke —

Thanks for the early feedback. Quick (internal + external) suggested compromise that tends to work for payments customers:

- Hosted (standard) service: keep 99.95% as measured at our API gateway (monthly). For Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private installs, we can commit to 99.99% provided AtlasPay meets the agreed sizing and traffic patterns in the order form. We’ll put the 99.99% option as an addendum with clear sizing-dependent clauses.
- Credits cap: we can move the cap to 100% of three months’ fees for customers who sign a 24-month commitment or higher. For annual or month-to-month, keep the 50% cap. The SLA_credits_table.xlsx includes both scenarios.
- Measurement methodology: see SLA_measurement_methodology.docx for precise rules — includes probe points, traffic-weighted regional calculations, and an audit log export path.
- Maintenance notice: we can accept 72-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance. Emergency maintenance still requires immediate notification and is limited to critical security patches.

Aditya — can you confirm the technical feasibility of the traffic-share credit approach and whether we can expose the required uptime dashboards to AtlasPay’s security team for the pilot?

If this sounds reasonable to you, Hannah and I will prep a short legal-ready summary to speed their GC review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message -----
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Luke Carr <luke@atlaspay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 13:02:07 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: SLA items for review & fallback credits

Luke / team —

Short technical notes on measurement and fallback behavior: 

- Measurement point: availability measured at the customer-facing API gateway (ingress) after any CDN. We compute per-region uptime, then weight by historical traffic share for the prior 30-day window to determine the effective monthly availability.
- Fallbacks: in a regional failure we will attempt cross-region routing for in-flight requests where latency allows. If cross-region routing is not possible due to regulatory constraints we will failover within the same region or to Dedicated nodes if provisioned.
- Credits math: example in SLA_credits_table.xlsx — if Region A (40% of traffic) is down for 60 minutes and Region B is healthy, the effective downtime for the account would be 0.4 * 60 minutes when calculating credits.
- Dashboard access: we can provide read-only dashboard access scoped to AtlasPay’s account team and a daily uptime feed (S3/CloudWatch export) for the pilot. Full audit exports require an approved DPA.

Attachment: SLA_measurement_methodology.docx (detailed rules and sample queries)

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the measurement queries.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message -----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Luke Carr <luke@atlaspay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: SLA items for review & fallback credits

Thanks all — quick summary and proposed next steps so we can get legal engaged and keep momentum: 

1) Pricing/commitment bridge: Redwood will offer the 99.99% Dedicated SLA as an addendum for customers who sign a 24-month commit (we’ll surface the costs in the addendum). Credits cap will move to 100% of three months’ fees for those commitments.
2) Measurement & evidence: we will include SLA_measurement_methodology.docx in the order form appendix and provide a read-only dashboard for the pilot.
3) Maintenance: Redwood agrees to 72-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance; emergency limited to critical security issues.
4) Next step: If AtlasPay legal can share a primary contact, Hannah/Marissa/legal will prepare a redline-ready summary and a short 30-min call to close. We’ll attach an updated Draft_OrderForm_redlines_v4.pdf to the next message and include a DocuSign link once mutual redlines are accepted.

Luke — can you share the name/email for your GC and preferred times for a 30-minute call on Friday (we are ET-friendly)?

Cheers,
Hannah
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs referenced: Draft_OrderForm_redlines_v3.pdf (redlines v3), SLA_credits_table.xlsx (calculation examples), SLA_measurement_methodology.docx (measurement details)]
